chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far from Abu Talib Abdillah ibn al-Salt from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, who is Dawud ibn Farqad, from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When the sun departs (from its zenith), the time for Dhuhr has entered, until the amount of time it takes for a person to pray four rak'ahs passes. When that time has passed, the time for Dhuhr and Asr has entered, until the amount of time it takes to pray four rak'ahs remains of the sun's light. When that amount remains, the time for Dhuhr has exited and the time for Asr remains until the sun sets."
ai.seo_question: What are the precise time boundaries for Dhuhr and Asr prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shia jurisprudential view of *Qasr al-Zaman* (shortening of time) for Dhuhr, distinguishing it from the Hanafi concept of *Jam'* (conjunction). It establishes that the specific window for Dhuhr alone ends when the shadow of an object equals its length (excluding zenith shadow), after which the time for both Dhuhr and Asr overlaps until sunset, reflecting the practical flexibility in prayer timing emphasized by the Imams.
